# `Q-18-12` — knitr Cache Is Off While Recording

> A knitr chunk asked for the cache, and Quarto turned it off for this run.

## What this means

**This note is no longer emitted.** A chunk that asks for knitr's cache now keeps it and is not
recorded; its finished markdown stays in the document.

The text below describes the earlier behavior.

Quarto records what each knitr chunk produced, so it can present the document without
running the chunks again. A chunk that hits knitr's cache is not run, so there would be
nothing to record. For that reason Quarto turns knitr's cache off for the run that records
the document, for every chunk that asked for it with `cache: true`.

The output is the same. The cost is time: a document that relies on `cache: true` runs those
chunks every time it is executed, and results that depend on state outside the document are
computed again. Existing cache directories are neither read nor deleted.

This is a note, not a problem: nothing needs fixing.

## How to change it

If a chunk is slow, keep its result in a file yourself (for example with `saveRDS()` and
`readRDS()`), or give the document a `freeze:` so it is not executed on every render.
